docs.title: About nams-registry
docs.text: This is a repository of NAM and NAM-adjacent sources collected in support of a NAMs landscape analysis.

docs.title: nams-registry
docs.text:
This is a repository of NAM and NAM-adjacent sources collected in support of a NAMs landscape analysis.

Sources are not limited to data repositories and knowledge bases. They also include reports, such as landscape analyses, reviews, and OECD Test Guidelines, and the scientific literature as a whole. A primary research paper is not a resource of its own: a NAM found in one names the scientific-literature resource and cites the paper on its NAM record.

URI: https://w3id.org/monarch-initiative/nams-registry

Name: nams-registry

    rank: 1000
    owner: Resource
    domain_of:
    - Resource
    range: HoldsNAMsEnum

      measurement methods for key events, but its primary content is adverse outcome

    rank: 1000
    owner: Resource
    domain_of:

    range: string
  curation_model:

    description: Who creates the resource's content, as the resource works today.
      Use more than one value when the resource mixes them.
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/monarch-initiative/nams-registry
    rank: 1000
    owner: Resource
    domain_of:
    - Resource
    range: CurationModelEnum
    multivalued: true
  dismech_integration:
    name: dismech_integration
    description: 'The resource''s current state in DisMech: whether any of its content
      has been incorporated into DisMech, and whether DisMech has tooling for it,
      such as a script or skill. Records what exists, not what the resource could
      offer. Free text for now.'
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/monarch-initiative/nams-registry
    rank: 1000
    owner: Resource
    domain_of:
    - Resource
    range: string
  supporting_scripts:
    name: supporting_scripts

      uses the resource without retrieving from it stays in dismech_integration.

    owner: Resource
    domain_of:
    - Resource
    range: SupportingScript
    multivalued: true
    inlined: true
    inlined_as_list: true
  priority:
    name: priority
    description: 'Extraction priority: how much the resource adds, and so how soon
      it is worth extracting content from. Set it once that has been investigated.
      A resource that repackages another one can still add value, for example through
      a new format, integration with other data, or easier access, so repackaging
      alone does not make a resource low priority.'
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/monarch-initiative/nams-registry
    rank: 1000
    owner: Resource
    domain_of:
    - Resource
    range: PriorityEnum
  priority_rationale:
    name: priority_rationale
    description: Why the resource was given its priority, based on what was found
      about what it adds. For a resource that repackages another, say what it adds
      beyond the original, or that nothing was found.

    rank: 1000
    owner: Resource
    domain_of:
    - Resource
    range: string
  extraction_effort:
    name: extraction_effort

    owner: Resource
    domain_of:
    - Resource

    domain_of:

    range: string

    name: activity_status

docs.text: The resource's current state in DisMech: whether any of its content has been incorporated into DisMech, and whether DisMech has tooling for it, such as a script or skill. Records what exists, not what the resource could offer. Free text for now.

docs.title: nams-registry
docs.text:
This is a repository of NAM and NAM-adjacent sources collected in support of a NAMs landscape analysis.

Sources are not limited to data repositories and knowledge bases. They also include reports, such as landscape analyses, reviews, and OECD Test Guidelines, and the scientific literature as a whole. A primary research paper is not a resource of its own: a NAM found in one names the scientific-literature resource and cites the paper on its NAM record.

URI: https://w3id.org/monarch-initiative/nams-registry

docs.title: Slot: part_of
docs.text: The ids of the registry Organization entries this resource belongs to, such as a database to the institute that runs it, or a core facility to its university. Set it on the part, not on the organization; an organization's parts are the entries that name it.

docs.title: Slot: path
docs.text: The file within the repository, e.g. scripts/fetch_namsnetwork.py. For a command of a larger tool, the file that defines it or configures it.

docs.title: Slot: priority
docs.text: Extraction priority: how much the resource adds, and so how soon it is worth extracting content from. Set it once that has been investigated. A resource that repackages another one can still add value, for example through a new format, integration with other data, or easier access, so repackaging alone does not make a resource low priority.

docs.title: Slot: priority_rationale
docs.text: Why the resource was given its priority, based on what was found about what it adds. For a resource that repackages another, say what it adds beyond the original, or that nothing was found.

docs.title: Slot: publications
docs.text: For a Report, the publications the report consists of. For any other resource, publications that describe the resource.

docs.title: Slot: relevance_note
docs.text: Why the resource was given its holds_nams value, e.g. "Holds the measurement methods for key events, but its primary content is adverse outcome pathways."

docs.title: Slot: repository
docs.text: The main version control repository for the resource, if it has one.

docs.title: Slot: resource_type
docs.text: What form the resource takes, such as a data source or a knowledge graph, or, for an organization covered as a whole, Organization. Imported from the KG-Registry category.

docs.title: Slot: source

docs.title: Slot: source_id
docs.text: The resource's identifier in the source registry, e.g. toxcast.

docs.title: Slot: source_url

docs.title: Slot: source_version
docs.text: The version of the source registry the content was copied from. For a registry kept in git, such as KG-Registry, the commit hash.

docs.title: Slot: supporting_scripts
docs.text: Scripts written to retrieve or parse the resource's content, in this repository or elsewhere. List only scripts that exist. DisMech tooling that uses the resource without retrieving from it stays in dismech_integration.

docs.title: Publication years in the Complement-ARIE Landscape Analysis
docs.text:
Written 2026-11-13 for the registry entries complement-arie-landscape-analysis (#36) and complement-arie-landscape-dashboard (#37). It asks when the papers in the Landscape Analysis were published, so that a review of them can be planned.

Sources:

  • The NIH Common Fund Complement-ARIE Landscape Analysis report, dated 29 February 2024. Its methods are on pages A-6 to A-12.
  • The "Q&A-Question Details" download from the report's Tableau Public dashboard, parsed with dismech's just complement-arie-parse. The download and the parser are described in dismech's landscape analysis report.
  • PubMed, for checking years and publication types.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
• The corpus is a recent snapshot, not a history of NAMs. Of the 2,737 papers with answers, 2,447 (89%) were published in 2023 and 10 in 2024. Only 3 were published before 2018.
  • That is how the corpus was searched. The Landscape Analysis searched reviews from 2018 onwards, and all papers only from 2023 onwards. A wider search was judged too large for the project.
  • Almost every paper from 2018–2022 is a review. 267 of the 276 with a PMID are indexed as reviews in PubMed. Papers from 2023–2024 are mostly primary research.
  • The years in the download are correct. All 40 papers in a random check had the same year in PubMed.
  • Publication year will not divide the review into useful parts. Splitting by question, or by the kind of paper, will.

docs.title: Publication years for each question
docs.text:
The download gives a year for each paper but no month or day, so the ranges below are in years. Counts are papers with an answer to the question, out of the 2,737 papers with answers. The years come from the paper's citation key (for example "Smith et al. 2023").

Question Papers answered Years Before 2020 2020–2022 2023 2024 Method Details Described 2,682 2004–2024 90 182 2,400 10 Method Technical Challenges Described 2,477 2004–2024 85 161 2,222 9 Method: New Technology or Refinement of Existing Approach 2,416 2004–2024 79 159 2,169 9 Tissue Types Examined 2,152 2004–2024 66 145 1,934 7 Remaining Challenges after Method Development 2,130 2004–2024 78 162 1,882 8 Cell Types Examined 1,961 2004–2024 59 135 1,761 6 Human Physiology Elements Considered 1,847 2004–2024 53 132 1,657 5 Disease(s) Examined 1,572 2017–2024 49 126 1,392 5 Method Limitations 1,498 2004–2024 51 121 1,321 5 Cellular Endpoints Measured 1,472 2004–2024 45 88 1,333 6 Method Validation Methods Described 1,391 2004–2024 29 54 1,302 6 Research Funding Details 1,303 2018–2024 24 85 1,190 4 Population Modeled 553 2018–2024 12 59 480 2 Model Metabolic Capacity Addressed 373 2018–2023 15 30 328 0 Economic Considerations Discussed 174 2018–2024 4 16 151 3 Ethical Considerations Discussed 119 2018–2023 3 8 108 0 Method Regulatory Use Discussed 96 2018–2023 4 9 83 0 Population Diversity and Variability Incorporated 48 2018–2023 3 9 36 0 Workforce Considerations Discussed 11 2020–2023 0 3 8 0

The ranges look wider than the corpus is. Most begin in 2004 because of two papers, and only three papers are older than 2018:

Paper PMID Year What it is Auld et al., Receptor Binding Assays for HTS and Drug Discovery 22553864 2004 A chapter of the NCBI Assay Guidance Manual Riss et al., Apoptosis Marker Assays for HTS 34339159 2004 A chapter of the NCBI Assay Guidance Manual Du et al., Progress in Mathematical Modeling of Gastrointestinal Slow Wave Abnormalities 29379448 2017 A review

Across all 2,737 papers, the years are 2004 (2), 2017 (1), 2018 (42), 2019 (48), 2020 (55), 2021 (61), 2022 (71), 2023 (2,447) and 2024 (10).

docs.title: Why the corpus is mostly from 2023
docs.text:
The Landscape Analysis ran two literature searches, and each had a date limit.

The initial search looked for reviews in PubMed, run on 10 October 2023 and returning 31,237 hits (page A-6):

We also limited the scope of the years (2018 to Present) and to reviews (as indexed by PubMed) only.

The broad search added Web of Science and Scopus and included all kinds of paper, run on 23 October 2023 and returning 67,718 hits after duplicates were removed (pages A-9 and A-10):

did not limit to reviews only, but we looked at only the most recently published papers (2023 – 2024 references published early).

The report gives the reason for the cutoff:

Expanding to 2018 – Present would have resulted in about 450k references, which was deemed beyond the project's scope given the focus on obtaining the most current perspective of NAMs in the scientific literature.

The years in the download match these two windows:

  • 2018–2022 (277 papers): found by the initial search, which took reviews only. 267 of the 276 with a PMID are indexed as reviews in PubMed.
  • 2023–2024 (2,457 papers): found mostly by the broad search. 768 of the 2,148 with a PMID are indexed as reviews, so most are primary research. The 2024 papers were published online early, before the search ran.
  • 2004 and 2017 (3 papers): outside both windows. The report also added 261 "seed studies" chosen by the project team (page A-11), and these three papers may be among them. That has not been checked.

Both searches ran in October 2023, so nothing published after that is included.

docs.title: Checking the years
docs.text: The year in each citation key was compared with PubMed for 40 papers chosen at random: 25 from 2023 and 15 from other years. All 40 matched PubMed's publication date or electronic publication date.

docs.title: What this means for reviewing the papers
docs.text:
• Read the corpus as NAMs literature from 2023, plus five years of reviews. It cannot show how NAMs developed over time, and it holds no papers published after October 2023.
  • Papers from before 2023 are almost all reviews. A review can point to several methods at once, while a 2023 paper usually describes one method. The two may be worth reviewing in different ways.
  • Divide the review by question, not by year. Year splits the corpus into 2023 and a small remainder. The questions split it more usefully. For example, "Disease(s) Examined" (1,572 papers) is the closest to the experimental models DisMech records.
  • Methods developed after October 2023 need another source. For NAMs published since then, the registry's other resources will be needed.

docs.title: How the counts were made
docs.text:
1. Download "Q&A-Question Details" from the dashboard's "Explore Questions" view, as described in dismech's data/complement-arie/MANIFEST.yaml.
  2. Run dismech's parser, which writes papers.tsv and answers.jsonl.
  3. For each question, take the answers that are not NA, look up each paper's year in papers.tsv, and count. Papers that group several papers under one key (merged_key=1) and papers with no answers (no_content=1) are left out, as in dismech's report.
  4. For review status, look up each PMID's publication types with PubMed's E-utilities esummary and count those that include "Review".
